justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are explicitly covered: Patient Registry Component captures demographics, Scheduling & Resource Component manages clash checks, EMR Management Component handles records, and Billing & Claims Component connects to payment clearinghouses.
justifications.performance_efficiency: EMR sub-second targets are supported by the frontend EMR View Engine using virtualization and local caching, Redis for clash checks, and Kafka for async domain events, though database read-scaling mechanisms are omitted.
justifications.compatibility: External interoperability is thoroughly addressed by the Interoperability Gateway via the FHIR API Facade Component, HL7 v2 to FHIR Adapter Component (Camel), and dedicated external payment gateway connectors.
justifications.usability: Distinct interfaces serve all user roles via Patient Portal (SPA) and Staff Dashboard (SPA), supporting operational flows with the Scheduling & Intake Controller and local draft preservation in Local Session State Manager.
justifications.reliability: While WebSocket Reconnection Manager and Kafka buffering are specified, there are no active-active data synchronization or cross-region replication mechanisms between on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1 to support 99.99% uptime.
justifications.security: HIPAA, GDPR, and R-05 are addressed via IdP MFA, mTLS via Istio, JWE envelope encryption, S3 KMS encryption with WORM Object Lock, Audit & Compliance Interceptor Component, and Break-Glass Authorization Component.
justifications.maintainability: Clear modular decomposition separates interoperability, gateway, and UI layers with well-defined contracts. However, Core Clinical & Billing Services aggregates multiple major business subdomains into a single container.
justifications.portability: Workloads are containerized, but targeting a hybrid deployment (on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1) is compromised by hard dependencies on AWS KMS and S3-specific primitives without specifying on-prem equivalents.

PERF-01.justification: EMR View Engine uses virtualized rendering and local caching, while API Gateway load balances traffic. However, backend database connection pooling and read-replica scaling under concurrent peak loads are not explicitly detailed.
sensitivity_points: API gateway routing latency under concurrent requests
Database read throughput for EMR queries
tradeoffs: Client-side caching improves render speed but risks viewing slightly stale clinical data

PERF-02.justification: FHIR API Facade and Apache Camel decouple ingestion via Kafka queues, shielding core clinical services from peak ingestion loads. Rate limiting at the gateway helps maintain EMR read performance under load.
elements: HL7 v2 to FHIR Adapter Component
sensitivity_points: Kafka ingestion throughput and queue partitioning
HAPI FHIR translation and validation overhead
tradeoffs: Asynchronous queue ingestion preserves core EMR performance at the cost of slight visibility latency

AVAIL-01.justification: Although active-active hybrid cloud is mandated, the architecture omits global server load balancing (GSLB) and cross-region database replication mechanisms needed to failover to on-prem within 1 minute without data loss.
sensitivity_points: Cross-region data replication latency and synchronization consistency
Global DNS or GSLB failover switching time
tradeoffs: Zero data loss across hybrid sites requires synchronous replication, increasing write latency

AVAIL-02.justification: Kafka enables asynchronous retry and decoupling, but synchronous pre-validation with external gateways without an explicit distributed transaction or outbox mechanism leaves in-flight claims vulnerable to mid-crash duplication.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency token implementation in billing requests
Database automated failover detection and promotion time
tradeoffs: Strict idempotency checks ensure exactly-once claim submission but add database lookup overhead

MOD-01.justification: Billing & Claims Component encapsulates clearinghouse integration, cleanly separated from EMR Management Component and other bounded contexts. Adding a clearinghouse requires modifications solely to the billing module.
sensitivity_points: Abstraction and modularity of external billing client interfaces
tradeoffs: Encapsulated external gateway integrations prevent cross-domain coupling across core services

MOD-02.justification: Changes are isolated to Patient Registry Component, Staff Dashboard (Scheduling & Intake Controller), and the interceptor/audit schema. The modular domain structure ensures EMR and Billing remain unaffected.
sensitivity_points: Flexibility of patient demographic schema and automated audit field extraction
tradeoffs: Strict regulatory auditing on new fields increases form validation complexity across tiers

SEC-01.justification: Authentication is delegated to an external IdP enforcing MFA. The API Gateway's Authentication & Authorization Filter validates tokens, while the Audit & Telemetry Interceptor records failures and triggers alerts via Kafka.
sensitivity_points: IdP token revocation propagation and policy enforcement latency
tradeoffs: Offloading auth to IdP centralizes MFA security but introduces an external dependency

SEC-02.justification: Access is evaluated by Open Policy Agent break-glass authorization, logged immutably via Kafka and Audit Interceptor, and long-term retention is guaranteed by S3-compatible storage with WORM Object Lock and AWS KMS.
sensitivity_points: OPA policy evaluation performance on record retrieval
Immutability enforcement through WORM Object Lock
tradeoffs: Auditing every single read operation incurs storage growth and marginal latency overhead

elements: HL7 v2 to FHIR Adapter Component
